acceptance: The four ambient git variable names are defined once, in internal/gitexec, and treefence imports them or the Isolated runner
treefence writes its snapshot trees through gitexec.TreeOfIndexCopy; its existing fence tests pass unchanged, and the allFiles behaviour on a missing index is a named test either way
No second copy of the index-copy routine remains (grep for os.Chtimes on an index copy finds only gitexec)
fix: Move treefence's snapshot onto gitexec.TreeOfIndexCopy and its git calls onto gitexec.Isolated (or give gitexec a seed-optional variant if the allFiles tolerance is still wanted, decided and pinned by a test), delete treefence's copyIndex and ambientGitVars, and keep ambientGitVars defined only in gitexec. treefence is the read-only phase fence (ADR-0097): land it as its own reviewed refactor, not inside a feature.
source: console lane cl-checkpoint, architecture re-review of evolve checkpoint, 2026-10-06
summary: evolve checkpoint added gitexec.Git.TreeOfIndexCopy (copy the worktree's index from one file handle keeping its mtime, run git add on the copy through GIT_INDEX_FILE, write-tree) and gitexec.Isolated (drops inherited GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR). internal/treefence still carries its own copy of both: writeTreeMode/copyIndex (go/internal/treefence/fence.go) and its ambientGitVars list, so the two four-name lists and the two copy routines can drift apart. The copies already differ in one way that matters: treefence's allFiles mode tolerates a failed real-index seed and builds the tree from an empty index, which TreeOfIndexCopy refuses.
title: treefence keeps a private copy of the scratch-index tree writer that gitexec now owns
